name: NUCLEO-G071RB (ST Nucleo-64 board, MB1360)
sources: STM32G071x8/xB datasheet DS12232 Rev 5 (features, Table 2 'RNG / AES: No / No', Table 26 run current); Nucleo-64 MB1360 user manual UM2324 Rev 5 (jumpers CN4, JP1, JP2, JP3, Table 12 ARDUINO pinout, Figure 3 top layout); both read on st.com 2026-10-07

columns.head: The chip: STM32G071RB
items: Runs the program, up to 64 million steps a second (64 MHz). Same core as the MSPM0 chips
Holds the program. Kept when the power is off
Working memory. 32 kB of it can be parity-checked; the rest cannot
The chip accepts 1.7 to 3.6 V; many pins also take 5 V

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: Serial text. USART2 goes to the Mac through the debug probe; USART1 is on the Arduino D0 and D1 pins
Two-wire sensor bus / fast bus for displays and memory chips
Makes a voltage, so the chip can test its own ADC with one wire
PWM for motors and LEDs; one 32-bit timer; one built for motor control
Checksums in hardware; moves data without the processor

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: ST-LINK debug probe on USB Micro-B, green LED LD4, blue button B1, reset button B2, 32.768 kHz crystal
ARDUINO Uno V3 sockets plus two rows of ST morpho pins that reach every chip pin
No AES or random-number hardware, no FPU, no math accelerator, no radio
The probe socket is Micro-B, not USB-C. LD4 shares pin PA5 with Arduino D13
